name: senior-mfs-ineligible
description: A married taxpayer filing separately is NOT eligible for the enhanced deduction for seniors, whatever their age - Schedule 1-A Part V requires a joint return. This fixture pinned and corrected the engine, which previously granted a single-style senior deduction to MFS filers.

source.publication: Schedule 1-A (Form 1040) 2025, Part V; Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), 'Enhanced deduction for seniors'
source.pin: Part V caution verbatim: 'If you are married, you must file a joint return with your spouse to claim this deduction.' The MFS filer still gets the $1,600 additional standard deduction for age 65+ (married amounts), but zero senior deduction.

derivation: Senior deduction = $0 (Part V caution: married filers must file jointly to claim it).
Additional standard deduction for 65+ at the MARRIED amount: $1,600. Standard deduction total = 15,750 + 1,600 = $17,350.
NIIT $0 (MAGI $50,000 below the $125,000 MFS threshold). Total tax $3,679.50.
